skip.reason: modal Desktop/Default/Small — the Small rung is density only in Figma (it is the same 588px wide as Medium); its header, body and footer are pinned by header-sm, body-sm and footer-sm. Whole-modal pixels are not compared because the component’s size="sm" also caps the width at 480px, an open design question recorded in the report.

modal Mobile/Default/Medium — the 350px mobile width is the viewport less the 16px margin on each side; a manifest fixture cannot set the viewport, so this breakpoint is checked through the Mobile story instead.
modal Desktop/Image-Based/Medium — identical to the Default modal except for its header, which image-md pins from 1825:3338.
modal Desktop/Image-Based/Small — header pinned by image-sm (1825:3565); the rest is the Small density covered by body-sm and footer-sm.
modal Mobile/Image-Based/Medium — the mobile breakpoint, unreachable from a fixture for the reason given for 230:5244.

.modal-header Medium/Center — not implemented: mud-modal has no centred-header option (Figma pads it 64px on the left and centres the title). Adding one is an API change, raised in the report rather than decided here.
.content-slot Type=Slot — a design-time placeholder whose own copy tells designers to detach it and build their content; it is not a runtime state of the component.
.modal-footer Default/Horizontal/1 action/Medium — the same footer box as the 2-action row footer-md pins, with one button fewer.
.modal-footer Default/Horizontal/1 action/Small — as 109:1965 at the Small rung, which footer-sm pins.
.modal-footer Default/Vertical/2 actions/Small — the stacked column footer-stacked pins, at the Small rung footer-sm pins.

.modal-footer Destructive/Horizontal/1/Medium — Figma draws identical footer chrome for Destructive; only the primary button turns #D92D20, and that colour belongs to mud-button variant="destructive", not to the modal.
.modal-footer Destructive/Vertical/2/Medium — as 365:17030, in the stacked column footer-stacked pins.

expect.note: Figma 111:2565 fills the set 230:5243 (620px designed, 16px padding) at 588px, radius 16, #FFFFFF, under Drop Shadow/400. The shadow’s third layer is a 0.5px spread hairline — not the 0.5px blur of Drop Shadow/300.

states.pixelNote: Two capture artefacts are neutralised, both because 111:2565 is the modal card alone, at rest. The backdrop is made transparent through its own token, since the Figma export has nothing but transparency around the card and the dimmed overlay would otherwise fill the whole 24px shadow bleed. And the body is clicked first: showModal() moves focus to the close button, and with no pointer input before it Chromium matches :focus-visible and draws a ring the resting design does not have — a user who opened the modal with a click never sees it.
